title: Quiet-launch ops weatherboard and KPI probes (WIP)
body:
Status: WIP notes + quick operational roadmap for a low-noise (quiet) launch. Purpose: provide a single-pane weatherboard for leaders + oncall during an initial limited rollout (alpha -> beta), with clear KPI probes, staffing scenarios, and canary decision logic.

Background / why this doc:
- We need to validate performance/cost signals without opening the floodgates.
- Objective is to detect regressions early and have guarded escalation triggers that are easy for non-engineering PMs to read.
- Target cohort: internal beta + 50 pilot customers over 30 days.

Scope (what's in this file):
- KPI definitions and probe thresholds
- Traffic/weatherboard scenarios (quiet, steady, surge-probe, degradation)
- Staffing runbook snippets for each scenario (who to call, escalation order)
- Canary checklist and rollback criteria (binary, easy decisions)
- Observability hooks to instrument before launch
- Open questions / follow-ups (owner + due date)

EXEC SUMMARY (one-paragraph):
Keep initial traffic limited to 1–5 rps per customer in the pilot, ramp by cohorts of 10. Track 4 primary probes: 95p latency (inference), token cost per 1k tokens, error-rate (5xx + model-confusion alerts), and amplification of retries (retry-loop detection). If any primary probe breaches soft threshold for >10 min AND secondary (error surface) is increasing, pause new cohort rollouts and flip fallback to smaller model variant.

KPI definitions (probes):
- inference_p95_ms: 95th percentile server-side latency for generation request (ms). soft_threshold=450ms; hard_threshold=900ms. owner: Diego Ramos.
- unit_token_cost_usd_per_k: end-to-end per-1k-token cost measured at request boundary (includes batching amortization estimate). soft_threshold=+$0.08 from baseline; hard_threshold=+$0.20. owner: Priya Desai.
- control_plane_5xx_rate_pct: percentage of requests returning 5xx (or service unavailable) at the API layer. soft_threshold=0.5% sustained; hard_threshold=2.0%. owner: Lina Gomez.
- model_confidence_regressions: measured by quality eval set (daily automated prompts). threshold: any single prompt drift > 15% metric drop triggers investigation. owner: Product QA (TBD).

Secondary signals (context):
- retry_amplification_ratio: (total requests / unique client requests) > 1.2 indicates retries.
- queue_depth_tail: number of requests queued > 95th percentile historical by region.
- infra_gpu_saturation_pct: average GPU util > 85% for 10+ min.

Traffic/weatherboard scenarios (how we visualize + read):
- Quiet (expected): 10 pilot customers, <200 qps combined. KPIs should be green; weekly baseline capture.
- Steady ramp: add 10 customers every 3 days, monitor p95 and cost. Soft threshold expected occasionally during the first 24h of a cohort.
- Surge-probe: synthetic burst test planned twice (pre-schedule): 2x normal for 15 minutes to validate autoscale. Run only during US-PST 10:00–14:00 window.
- Degradation (failure mode): sustained p95>hard OR 5xx_rate>hard OR model quality regression. In that case, enact rollback to pinned model variant and reduce traffic by 70%.

Staffing scenarios (quick):
- Green / Quiet: 1 product ops lead (Aisha), oncall SRE (Lina), engineer on slack watch (Diego). No page.
- Yellow / Soft breach (soft_threshold exceeded for 10+ min): product ops ping channel #quiet-launch, SRE triages, engineering standby 1 hour. Slack escalation: @SRE-oncall -> @infra-sre.
- Red / Hard breach or multiple signals: page SRE primary, product lead, and infra engineer. Escalation order: SRE primary -> Infra oncall -> Serving runtime lead -> Product director. Page policy doc: link in linked_artifacts.

Canary checklist (pre-rollout must-haves):
- [ ] Pin fallback model variant available and smoke-tested (owner: Diego).
- [ ] Synthetic probe harness deployed in prod region and running (owner: Lina).
- [ ] Observability dashboards: inference_p95, cost per 1k tokens, 5xx rate, retry ratio (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Alerting: soft alerts to slack; hard alerts to pager (owner: SRE).
- [ ] Runbook snapshot up-to-date with contact list and runbook id (owner: Product Ops).
- [ ] Legal/Privacy checklist signed for pilot customer set (owner: Legal).

Rollback decision rubric (simple):
- If ANY hard_threshold breached AND either (retry_ratio rising OR infra_gpu_saturation > 90%), then rollback to previously pinned model variant and reduce incoming traffic to 30% of pre-breach level.
- Notify customers in pilot cohort within 30 minutes of rollback. Template: linked_artifacts Confluence doc.

Observability hooks (instrumentation checklist):
- request_id attached at edge and propagated to logs (done: infra/pr-312)
- token-count annotation on every generation event (TODO)
- per-request routing metadata (model_variant, quantization_profile) included in traces (owner: Diego)
- daily automated eval run against benchmark prompt set; web hook to product-qa results (owner: Product QA)

Low-friction experiments to run during quiet launch (ideas):
- Sampled prefix caching experiment (10% traffic) to measure token cost savings with minimal latency impact.
- Small-model fallback trial for non-critical endpoints (customer support snippets) to get cost delta.

Open questions / action items:
- Who owns the daily quality-eval gating? (ASSIGN: Product QA) due: 2026-03-05
- Confirm SLA language for pilot customers (Legal) due: 2025-10-01
- Finalize synthetic surge schedule w/ infra (owner: Lina) due: 2025-09-24
- Add cost-threshold alert to billing pipeline (owner: Priya) due: 2025-10-05

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the language simple for oncall: "pause new cohorts" instead of "gradual rollback".
- Keep the first two weeks manual-cadence to learn failure modes; automation later.

Appendix: quick contact roster (for runbook paste)
- Product Ops: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)
- Infra SRE: Lina Gomez (lina@redwood.ai)
- Serving Runtime: Diego Ramos (diego@redwood.ai)
- Cost/Product: Priya Desai (priya@redwood.ai)

Revision history:
- 2025-09-17: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-10-02: added KPI thresholds + staffing (collab: Lina)
- 2026-02-28: updated rollback rubric and added open questions (in_review)

END.
